title: The book they were racing
subtopic: T3 — Around the World in Eighty Days, and the serial that ran in real time
learning_goal: Know the book's title, author and date, and that it was serialised so its ending fell on the real calendar — which is why readers bet on it.

narration.script: So who were they racing? A book. Around the World in Eighty Days, by Jules Verne. It ran as a serial in the Paris newspaper Le Temps, starting on the sixth of November, eighteen seventy-two — while, inside the story, Fogg was out there doing it. And Verne timed the ending to land on the real calendar. The instalments ran up to the twentieth of December. On the twenty-first — Fogg's deadline — there was nothing at all. The last two chapters appeared on the twenty-second. Some readers thought it was actually happening. Bets were placed. Shipping companies wrote to Verne asking to be put in it. The book came out complete six weeks later, and it has never been out of print since.

review.notes:
ADDED 2026-09-09 on founder feedback: "i didnt see a good intro of verne and his book title i think thats necessary for a series on just that book." Correct — the episode named Verne twice in passing and never once said what he wrote.
The serialisation facts (Le Temps from 6 Nov 1872; instalments timed so 21 Dec, Fogg's deadline, carried none; last two chapters 22 Dec; readers betting; companies lobbying to appear; Hetzel book 30 Jan 1873) are F-N13/F-N14, researched 2026-09-09 from the novel's Wikipedia article and NOT yet through Fact-Check.
Placed between the racers and the wager so "who were they racing?" is answered with the book before the bet is described.
